edges.description: ZMPSTE24 performs the final cleavage that converts prelamin A to lamin A.
Farnesyl-prelamin A deforms the nucleus; halving its level in Zmpste24-null cells makes misshapen nuclei less frequent.
Unprocessed prelamin A impairs recruitment of 53BP1 and RAD51 to DNA lesions, delaying checkpoint response and repair.
edges.target: Defective DNA Damage Response and Genomic Instability

edges.description: A route independent of nuclear shape: farnesyl-methyl prelamin A at the nuclear rim suppresses AKT-mTOR signalling, promoting senescence.
Defective prelamin A processing produces aging-like bone loss in the mouse; the cellular steps in between are not established.
edges.target: Skeletal Stem/Progenitor Cell Loss and Impaired Bone Formation

edges.description: Proposed from the clinical pattern: the membranous interparietal bone fails to ossify while the endochondral supraoccipital forms normally.
Farnesyl-prelamin A in adipocytes reduces fat stores only modestly in the mouse, so most of the fat loss may arise elsewhere.
The nuclear abnormalities activate a p53-dependent checkpoint.
Delayed DNA repair drives early cellular senescence.

edges.limitations: Adipocyte-specific deletion reduces fat only modestly and only in males, so the global-knockout lipodystrophy may be secondary to systemic disease.

nodes.description: Lipoatrophy is part of the defining phenotype, generalized in about half of patients. Zmpste24-null mice lose almost all adipose tissue by four months, but deleting Zmpste24 only in adipocytes reduces fat only modestly, so whether the lipodystrophy is cell-autonomous is unresolved.

nodes.description: Zmpste24-deficient cells accumulate DNA damage and chromosome aberrations, are sensitive to DNA-damaging agents, and fail to recruit 53BP1 and RAD51 to lesions, associated with hypoacetylation of histone H4 at lysine 16. Demonstrated in mouse cells; not yet measured in MADB patient cells.

evidence.snippet: We found that Zmpste24-deficient mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) show increased DNA damage and chromosome aberrations and are more sensitive to DNA-damaging agents.

evidence.reference_title: Histone H4 lysine 16 hypoacetylation is associated with defective DNA repair and premature senescence in Zmpste24-deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: Specifically, histone H4 was hypoacetylated at a lysine 16 residue (H4K16), and this defect was attributed to the reduced association of a histone acetyltransferase, Mof, to the nuclear matrix.

nodes.description: The interparietal part of the occipital squama, which forms by membranous ossification, fails to ossify, while the endochondral supraoccipital forms normally. Delayed suture closure and wide fontanelles fit the same membranous-bone pattern, but no study has tested that link.

nodes.description: Variable and uncommon in the ZMPSTE24 form. Diabetes was diagnosed in one adult with a homozygous missense allele, and impaired glucose tolerance and diabetes are reported in a few patients, but other reports found no metabolic disturbance and none of the living Surinamese patients was diabetic. Metabolic complications are more typical of the LMNA type A form.

nodes.description: The farnesyltransferase inhibitor lonafarnib is FDA-approved for processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies. It corrects the nuclear phenotype of MADB patient fibroblasts. Another farnesyltransferase inhibitor, ABT-100, improves the Zmpste24-null mouse, while FTI-277 failed in one fibroblast study. No clinical outcome data in MADB patients are available.

evidence.reference_title: The farnesyl transferase inhibitor (FTI) lonafarnib improves nuclear morphology in ZMPSTE24-deficient fibroblasts from patients with the progeroid disorder MAD-B.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, and in contrast to a previous report, we show here that FTI treatment also improves the aberrant nuclear phenotypes in MAD-B patient cells with mutations in ZMPSTE24 (P248L or L425P).

evidence.reference_title: The farnesyl transferase inhibitor (FTI) lonafarnib improves nuclear morphology in ZMPSTE24-deficient fibroblasts from patients with the progeroid disorder MAD-B.

Nuclear shape is a marker rather than a sufficient cause: fibroblasts from a restrictive dermopathy patient with only prelamin A had few nuclear abnormalities, and several rescues improve disease without normalizing nuclei.

nodes.description: Zmpste24-null mice have fewer osteoblasts and osteocytes, more marrow fat, reduced cortical and trabecular bone and spontaneous fractures. Conditional deletion places the lesion upstream of mature osteoblasts: removing Zmpste24 from Prx1-lineage skeletal stem/progenitor cells causes bone loss, while removing it from Osx-lineage osteoblasts does not.

evidence.snippet: We now show compound heterozygous mutations, Phe361fsX379 and Trp340Arg, in the zinc metalloproteinase (ZMPSTE24) gene in one of the four patients who had severe MAD associated with progeroid appearance and generalized lipodystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Mandibuloacral dysplasia type B (MADB): a cohort of eight patients from Suriname with a homozygous founder mutation in ZMPSTE24 (FACE1), clinical diagnostic criteria and management guidelines.
evidence.snippet: All the Surinamese patients are of African descent and share the same homozygous c.1196A > G, p.(Tyr399Cys) missense variant in the ZMPSTE24 gene, confirming MADB.

nodes.description: Biallelic ZMPSTE24 variants reduce, but do not abolish, the activity of the ER and inner nuclear membrane zinc metalloprotease. Missense alleles reduce catalytic activity, protein stability, or both. Residual activity orders the ZMPSTE24 disease spectrum: none in restrictive dermopathy, partial in MADB and severe progeria.

evidence.reference_title: Zinc metalloproteinase, ZMPSTE24, is mutated in mandibuloacral dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: We now show compound heterozygous mutations, Phe361fsX379 and Trp340Arg, in the zinc metalloproteinase (ZMPSTE24) gene in one of the four patients who had severe MAD associated with progeroid appearance and generalized lipodystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Zinc metalloproteinase, ZMPSTE24, is mutated in mandibuloacral dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: The ZMPSTE24 mutant construct, Phe361fsX379, was inactive in complementing the yeast a-factor but the mutant, Trp340Arg, was partially active compared to the wild type ZMPSTE24 construct.

evidence.reference_title: Human ZMPSTE24 disease mutations: residual proteolytic activity correlates with disease severity.
evidence.snippet: Complete loss-of-function alleles are associated with RD, whereas retention of partial, measureable activity results in MAD-B or severe progeria.

evidence.reference_title: ZMPSTE24 missense mutations that cause progeroid diseases decrease prelamin A cleavage activity and/or protein stability.
evidence.snippet: All mutations show diminished prelamin A processing and fall into three classes, with defects in activity, protein stability or both.

nodes.description: Zmpste24 deficiency upregulates p53 target genes with cellular senescence and organismal accelerated ageing; these are largely rescued by halving Lmna dosage and partly reversed by p53 loss. Patient fibroblasts show reduced proliferation and lifespan. Senescence is not simply a consequence of nuclear shape: reducing ICMT or RCE1 activity in Zmpste24-deficient cells relieves senescence through prelamin A-dependent AKT-mTOR signalling without correcting misshapen nuclei.

evidence.reference_title: Accelerated ageing in mice deficient in Zmpste24 protease is linked to p53 signalling activation.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that Zmpste24 deficiency elicits a stress signalling pathway that is evidenced by a marked upregulation of p53 target genes, and accompanied by a senescence phenotype at the cellular level and accelerated ageing at the organismal level.

evidence.reference_title: Accelerated ageing in mice deficient in Zmpste24 protease is linked to p53 signalling activation.
evidence.snippet: These phenotypes are largely rescued in Zmpste24-/-Lmna+/- mice and partially reversed in Zmpste24-/-p53-/- mice.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting isoprenylcysteine methylation ameliorates disease in a mouse model of progeria.
evidence.snippet: The reduced ICMT activity caused prelamin A mislocalization within the nucleus and triggered prelamin A-dependent activation of AKT-mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling, which abolished the premature senescence of Zmpste24-deficient fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting RAS-converting enzyme 1 overcomes senescence and improves progeria-like phenotypes of ZMPSTE24 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: These results strengthen the idea that the presence of misshapen nuclei does not prevent phenotype improvement and suggest that targeting RCE1 might be useful for treating the rare progeroid disorders associated with ZMPSTE24 deficiency.
